text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: INC-7234 fired for canary-auth-checks (service: inference-canary). Trigger: 5xx auth failures from canary cluster in us-west-2. Auto-page sequence started.

pd-bot: PagerDuty note: page delivered to oncall (michaela). Attempting auto-ack if detected heartbeat.

michaela: ack  — I'm on it. 1) canary pool showing ~18% 500s from auth service, token exchange failing, 2) production stable outside canaries so far. tagging eng-release and SRE.

jonah: seeing similar spikes in the canary telemetry stream. dumping recent logs now:```\nkubectl logs -n inference canary-auth-0 --since=10m | grep -i token
2026-03-15T02:12:03Z ERROR auth: token exchange failed status=403 detail=\"invalid key\"
2026-03-15T02:12:05Z WARN auth: retrying token refresh
```

kevin: rolling feature-flag pushed in last deploy toggles new auth backend (ff:auth-v3). Canary instances got the new path. If that's broken we should rollback flag.

michaela: good catch. can someone confirm if the ff rollout is staged via config service or baked in deploy? @eng-release?

eng-release: it was pushed via config rollout at 02:10 UTC, targeting 5% canary pool only. We have the flag id: ff/auth/backend=v3. We did not change service account keys.

samir: quick mitigation plan: 1) flip ff to v2 for canary targets only, 2) if flip fails, block traffic to canary and re-route to stable. Who can flip the flag? @kevin?

kevin: I can flip it now via prod-config CLI. Running:```\nprod-config set ff/auth/backend=v2 --scope canary --reason \"revert canary auth backend after 5xx spike\" --author kevin
```

kevin: done. config change pushed to canary at 02:15:30Z. Watching telemetry...

jonah: telemetry update: 5xx rate dropping — was 18% -> 3% in the last 2 mins. latency ok. No customer-facing errors reported yet.

michaela: good. I'll keep PD in the loop. Any PagerDuty escalation history? pd-bot, did it escalate to the next rotation?

pd-bot: page auto-escalation suppressed — page was acked by michaela within 90s, no further escalation. Logging incident timeline.

product-ops: any customers pinging support? I'm watching support queue. No inbound tickets mentioning auth failures right now.

michaela: marking impact: degraded canary only, no broad customer impact detected. Root cause hypothesis: new auth backend (ff v3) had an env mismatch for token audience. We'll open a follow-up with eng-release to validate config matrix.

eng-release: confirmed — config rollout accidentally omitted audience override for canary. That explains 403s. Creating PR to require explicit audience mapping in rollout tooling.

samir: next steps: 1) postmortem ticket (ENGINC-9802) assigned to eng-release, 2) improve preflight checks for auth FFs, 3) add runbook note about immediate ff flip path.

michaela: transferring to next oncall for monitoring — jonah, take handoff for 02:30-04:30UTC. I'll update the incident record and close the PD incident once stable for 30m. cc @product-ops for customer comms decision.

jonah: taking handoff. I'll keep an eye on canary and throttle alerts. If we see >5% 500s again, we'll initiate canary isolation.

michaela: incident summary: cause=feature-flagged auth backend missing audience override for canary, mitigation=flip flag to v2, impact=canary 5xx spike, customers unaffected. PD incident INC-7234: acknowledged -> mitigated. Will create postmortem draft after shift. :white_check_mark:

pd-bot: PD incident update: INC-7234 status updated to \"mitigated\" by michaela at 02:22:15Z.

incident-bot: Logging thread to incident channel and creating timeline entry. Remember to add telemetry graphs and the relevant config diff to the postmortem.

kevin: added the config diff link: https://prod-config.internal/changesets/ff-auth-3345004321. Also adding the rollback command snippet to runbook.

product-ops: we'll prepare a short blameless note for customers if asked, but no outreach required now.

michaela: closing thread for now; jonah please re-open if any regression. Thanks team. :tada:
